title: Application for Federal Assistance (SF-424)
description: The SF-424 application cover: organization and contact information, project and funding details, State review, debt disclosure, certification and authorized representative. This is a source-reconciled plan proposal; no maintained TypeSpec definition is included.

children.help_text: 21. *By signing this application, I certify (1) to the statements contained in the list of certifications** and (2) that the statements herein are true, complete and accurate to the best of my knowledge. I also provide the required assurances** and agree to comply with any resulting terms if I accept an award. I am aware that any false, fictitious, or fraudulent statements or claims may subject me to criminal, civil, or administrative penalties. (U.S. Code, Title 18, Section 1001) ** The list of certifications and assurances, or an internet site where you may obtain this list, is contained in the announcement or agency specific instructions.

notes: Plan-first proposal for FID713 SF424_4_0 v4.0, reconciled with the pinned DAT/XSD and existing SGG SF424_v4_0. The previous 41-field catalogue outline omitted contact, applicant-type, agency/opportunity, project, State-review and disclosure fields and contained obsolete XML paths. This plan reuses the preserved complete source draft and current SGG answer names, rather than defining a new contract.

JSON answer paths follow the existing SGG schema: applicant is the address, contact_person and authorized_representative are names, and other answer names remain as currently installed. UI headings are not extra data containers. This preserves compatibility for the first definition; a later semantic regrouping requires a concrete reviewed benefit and migration cost.

DAT09-0/09-1/09-2 and XSD ApplicantTypeCode1/2/3 are one ordered list of one to three different codes, matching existing SGG applicant_type_code. Finite source bindings preserve each source position without three duplicated questions. Preserve unique selections and the conditional Other explanation; this plan is not executable validation.

ContactPerson is optional as an XSD container, while DAT08-f02/08-f04 and current SGG require its first and last names. The plan proposes preserving existing SGG/DAT requiredness, with an explicit upstream discrepancy against XSD. No acceptance of this policy is inferred.

Country defaults to USA from DAT08-d7; US addresses require State and ZIP, with a nine-character US ZIP minimum in DAT08-d8 in addition to the generic XSD one-to-thirty bound. Province is optional, enabled only for non-US addresses. Preserve supplied non-US answers; state/province wire exclusivity and inactive answer handling require later tests and Billy XML decisions.

The seven funding values use exact XSD nonnegative bounds and cent precision; the total has a larger maximum than each input. Proposed examples use decimal strings to match existing SGG capture. The current shared SGG monetary-string schema admits negative values and differs in capacity; compilation/schema admission alone cannot resolve this source-policy mismatch.

DateReceived, AORSignature and DateSigned are required wire values supplied by submission/signing, not editable applicant fields. UEI and agency/opportunity/competition data use current cover/context population. DAT06-1 and07-0 are optional entered values; existing SGG describes them as State-owned but leaves them editable. Their ownership remains a review question, not a new read-only restriction.

DAT18-g explicitly calculates the sum of18a through18f. Existing SGG uses sum_monetary. This differs from R&R DAT15-3, which asks the applicant to enter the combined total; do not generalize calculation ownership across forms.

Certification source statement and announcement-specific certifications/assurances instructions are retained with section21. DAT requires checking I Agree; existing SGG schema accepts either boolean value. An affirmative submission gate needs explicit behavior tests and human source-policy review.

State-review options retain exact XSD casing. Existing SGG stores lowercase state in options a/b and explicitly normalizes it to State during XML generation. Proposed and existing Data examples are therefore distinguished; no new XML transform is implemented.

Attachments remain four distinct questions/purposes: areas affected, additional project-title documents (up to100), additional congressional districts and conditional debt explanation. UUIDs in examples illustrate existing SGG references only; no upload, file identity/ownership, submission or generated XML is asserted.

All source input rows and option labels are retained in the reviewed inventory; non-input headings/navigation/burden controls are not extra answer fields. risks: Review source-versus-SGG differences before definition acceptance: required contact names under optional XSD ContactPerson; US ZIP minimum; monetary sign/capacity; affirmative certification; State-owned optional fields; county visibility; StateReview code casing. Existing behavior is evidence, not automatic source-policy approval.

Revision uses the existing scalar Select options, including AC/AD/BC/BD combinations. No new widget is required by this plan. Test Revision activation, E explanation, Continuation/Revision award identifier and inactive-answer retention/omission in the later definition.

Existing SGG source schema, UI, rule schema, XML mapping and fixtures are pinned separately. Authenticated population, signing, save/reload, uploads, API integration and successful submission have not been exercised by this plan-only work.

Static source comparison accounts for fields, supported constraints, labels/help and source positions; it does not execute date ordering, uniqueness, conditional obligations, calculation, affirmative consent, XML xs:choice or totalDigits. No compiled maintained TypeSpec form is included.
